title: Recruiter handbook — candidate quality & onboarding playbook
content:
Purpose: This is a lightweight, recruiter-facing playbook for consistent candidate quality signals from sourcing through the first 90 days. It combines quick interview-evidence templates, a simple numeric rubric to normalize scoring, and a compact first-week/first-90-day handoff checklist for hiring managers.

Audience: Recruiters, sourcers, hiring managers, interviewers. Not intended to replace role-specific hiring criteria (see role templates), but to standardize how we capture evidence and hand off candidates into onboarding.

Quick notes to self:
- Keep evidence short — 2–3 bullet examples per skill.
- Capture both signal and risk (e.g., "strong async communication" vs "limited experience with infra scale").
- When in doubt, ask hiring manager for the one non-negotiable skill.

1) Sourcing -> Screen: 5 mandatory screening checkpoints (quick yes/no + example evidence)
- Role fit: 1–2 sentences on primary domain experience ("built search infra for e-commerce, 3y").
- Impact level: signal of ownership ("launched feature used by 200k MAU vs contributed to team library").
- Communication: short async sample or phone screen clarity ("clear, structured answers; good follow-ups").
- Dealbreakers: items from job doc (visa, comp expectations mismatch, non-starter tech gaps).
- Culture/team fit: one positive data point (e.g., mentoring, shipping cross-functional).

Template: Screening note (one paragraph)
- One-line role summary: "Senior Backend engineer — search infra, 3y at X"
- Top signals: 1) Ship/impact 2) Architectural depth 3) Communication
- Key risk: "Limited cloud ops experience; willing to learn"
- Suggested next step: "Onsite loop with infra + hiring manager"

2) Interview evidence capture (standardized log) — use this for every loop
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [role] | Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Interviewer: [name] | Round: [take-home / system design / behavioral]
- Short rubric scores (1-5) as separate fields: Technical depth, Problem solving, System design, Communication, Team fit
- Evidence bullets (2–4): exact phrasing from candidate or paraphrase with timestamped example
- Concise risk: single-line ("needs ramp on distributed tracing")
- Recommendation: Hire / No hire / Hire with mentorship / Needs more data

Scoring guidance (keep short):
- 5 = exceptional (can own and mentor others immediately)
- 4 = strong (meets expectations with little ramp)
- 3 = solid (meets most expectations; requires light ramp)
- 2 = concerning (gaps in core area)
- 1 = clear no (does not meet role baseline)

3) Interview rubric examples (copy/paste friendly)
- Tech depth (1–5): examples to look for: specific architecture choices, tradeoffs, memory/time complexity, tradeoffs between async/sync, reasons for library choices.
- System design (1–5): looks for scope, API boundaries, failure modes, scalability estimates, simple latency/cost calculations.
- Problem solving (1–5): approaches complexity, decomposes problems, tests assumptions, writes pseudo-code or clear steps.
- Communication (1–5): explains tradeoffs, asks clarifying Qs, concisely summarizes.
- Team fit (1–5): cross-team collaboration examples, feedback loops, mentorship.

4) Hiring manager handoff template (pre-offer and pre-day-1)
- Before offer: key negotiation levers (title, level, comp band), expected start date, visa/relocation notes, role one-pager.
- Offer email draft: short, highlights role, manager, start date, one-sentence on why hire.
- Day-1 packet to Manager: candidate scorecard, 3 focus goals for first 30 days, suggested mentor, suggested learning resources.

Example 30-day focus goals (suggested by recruiter):
- Week 1: environment, access, meet core team, simple bug fix -> merge
- Weeks 2–4: own small component, ship a non-user-facing improvement, attend on-call rotation shadow

5) First-week checklist for people-ops -> hiring manager handoff (copy/paste to new hire doc)
- Access: corp email, repo, CI, monitoring dashboard, Slack, calendar invites for core syncs
- Admin: payroll/kickoff, benefits FAQ link, KYC/ID verification status
- Introductions: schedule 1:1s with manager (30m), mentor (30m), cross-functional partner (15m)
- Quick wins: assign a small PR or doc to review and ship in week 1

6) 30/60/90 quick rubric for manager check-ins (one-liner fields)
- 30d: understanding of codebase, delivered first small ship, integration with team rituals
- 60d: ownership of a project with measurable outcome, proactive in async comms, feedback loop established
- 90d: independent delivery, mentoring newer hires, measurable impact metric (reduce latency X% / increase throughput Y%)

7) Example interview evidence (do this verbatim when you can)
- "When I added client-side dedupe we saw a 12% reduction in duplicate requests; I measured post-change with trace sampling and alerted on error rates while rolling out" — good system signal
- "Led hiring for the infra team; owned on-call rota and reduced mean time to recovery by implementing automated rollbacks" — strong ownership signal

8) Red flags log (one-line):
- Overclaims without detail (ask for a concrete example)
- Can't explain an architecture they claim to have built
- Repeated inability to reason about tradeoffs

9) Messaging templates (recruiter -> interviewer -> manager)
- To interviewer (pre-loop): short context, what we need to validate, two bullets of desired evidence, time block.
- To hiring manager (post-offer): scorecard + short note with recommended ramp plan and top 2 areas to monitor in first 30d.

10) Open questions + items to finalize (notes, keep as TODO at top of doc)
- Should we require an asynchronous coding sample for remote senior hires? pros/cons list needed.
- Define exact comp band phrasing for external offers (legal review pending).
- Consolidate role-specific rubric variants in a shared sheet (link to product/infra lists).

Appendix: Quick copyable templates (put into ATS notes)
- Screening snippet: "[Candidate] — Senior Backend. Built search infra at X. Strong on architecture and ownership; potential gap in cloud operations. Recommend onsite."
- Interview request to candidate: short logistics template included in ATS (time zones, loop participants).

References: Link to role templates folder (Confluence), hiring manager checklist (JIRA-HR-367), candidate experience survey template (Mural link).

Footer: Keep this doc short and editable. Recruiters: paste evidence into ATS after every loop. Hiring managers: add 3 measurable success criteria before week 1.

Last updated: 2025-11-10 by Maya Chen

[Notes: informal, may include shorthand in ATS; this is intentionally conversational for speed. Document will be iterated after pilot with two hiring squads in Q1 2026.]
